title: OpenAPI to MCP: what it uses
lede: One arrow for each component this feature lists. The steps reuse the feature's own "how it works" text; nothing here is a new claim. Internal and confidential: this text comes from an internal Ping deck and has not been tested on our tenant.

steps.title: OpenAPI specification
steps.what: Privilege takes an existing OpenAPI specification and launches an MCP server for that API.
steps.why: Agents speak MCP but enterprise capability lives in REST APIs, so every exposure demands a development project.

steps.title: Per-operation tools
steps.what: Each operation becomes a callable tool with a clean per-operation schema, with parameters, types and descriptions taken from the spec, so the tool surface stays in step with the API definition.
steps.why: Agents speak MCP but enterprise capability lives in REST APIs, so every exposure demands a development project.

steps.title: Managed container per spec
steps.what: The generated server runs as its own managed container per specification, with no server code to write, host or operate, and it is then fronted by the gateway as an ordinary MCP application with the same controls as any hosted server.
steps.why: Agents speak MCP but enterprise capability lives in REST APIs, so every exposure demands a development project.

steps.title: Gateway per-tool policy
steps.what: Requests pass through per-tool policy and entitlement-aware discovery, and the credential the API expects is injected at request time from the application configuration or the calling user's vault.
steps.why: Agents speak MCP but enterprise capability lives in REST APIs, so every exposure demands a development project.

steps.title: Entitlement-aware discovery
steps.what: Requests pass through per-tool policy and entitlement-aware discovery, and the credential the API expects is injected at request time from the application configuration or the calling user's vault.
steps.why: Agents speak MCP but enterprise capability lives in REST APIs, so every exposure demands a development project.

steps.title: Credential injection
steps.what: Requests pass through per-tool policy and entitlement-aware discovery, and the credential the API expects is injected at request time from the application configuration or the calling user's vault.
steps.why: Agents speak MCP but enterprise capability lives in REST APIs, so every exposure demands a development project.

steps.title: Header-based backend auth
steps.what: Authentication to the backend is header-based, so static headers or injected credentials pass through to the API, while login flows and session tokens remain the calling agent's responsibility by design.
steps.why: Agents speak MCP but enterprise capability lives in REST APIs, so every exposure demands a development project.
